subject: Persistent 429 wave — unintended retry amplification / next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@federalgrid.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 429/timeout errors from Redwood — immediate help needed

Mina,

We started seeing a sustained wave of 429 responses and client timeouts against our integration this morning around 08:45 PT. Attached is a flame-graph-like screenshot from our dashboard showing a sharp uptick in retries and a subsequent drop in successful calls. Latency for completed calls has also doubled. Our side is configured with the stock Redwood SDK (v1.2.0) and an in-house polling loop for batch requests.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (rate limits, routing, capacity) or whether this looks like behavior from our end? This is affecting our production billing and user experience.

Attachments: screenshot-429-graph.png, sdk-config.txt

Thanks,
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Integrations, FederalGrid

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@federalgrid.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 429/timeout errors from Redwood — immediate help needed

Hi Sarah — thanks for the report and the screenshot. I've looped in Monica (Customer Success) to coordinate.

Quick summary of what I'm doing now:
- Looking at ingress metrics and recent deploys for FederalGrid.
- Checking for any routing or global rate-limit changes that could explain 429s.
- Asking infra to surface per-customer token-level spikes and queue lengths.

From a first glance the pattern in your graph (sharp retry spikes followed by errors) could indicate a client-side retry amplification: if the client retries aggressively without jitter that can create a feedback loop and produce the 429 wave you describe. I don't want to assume, though — we'll validate server-side.

I'll follow up within 30 mins with what we see and recommended immediate mitigations.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: FederalGrid 429 wave — initial triage

Internal notes (do not forward):
- Infra indicates a ~3x increase in request rate from keys tied to FederalGrid starting 08:40 PT. 95th percentile latency rose from 120ms -> 320ms across a subset of pods. Error breakdown: 64% 429, 28% 504/timeout, 8% 5xx.
- No new Redwood deploys or rate-limit policy changes in the last 24h that would explain a config drift.
- Server-side token buckets are showing transient exhaustion for several endpoints — consistent with burst amplification.

Suggested immediate actions (short-term):
1) Put an application-level soft throttling rule for FederalGrid to shed excess traffic and stabilize the cluster (return 429-fast when above threshold to avoid queueing).
2) Apply an automatic circuit-breaker at the edge for their key when error-rate > 30% for 1 minute.
3) Ask FederalGrid to temporarily reduce concurrency from their side and to add randomized exponential backoff with jitter; provide a recommended patch/snippet.
4) Schedule a postmortem and make an SDK config change to default to safer backoff parameters in next release (medium term).

I'll stand up the soft throttle now if Mina approves.

-Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: FederalGrid 429 wave — initial triage

Do the throttle and circuit-breaker now. Also draft a concise message for Sarah with immediate steps they can take (priority: stop tight loops, upgrade SDK, apply backoff snippet). Loop Rishi for exec awareness — this may need credits/comp consideration if we impact SLAs.

-Mina

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@federalgrid.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 429/timeout errors from Redwood — immediate help needed

Sarah — quick update and actions we've taken: 

What we saw (summary):
- Sudden amplification in request rate for your API key starting ~08:40 PT, with many in-flight retries.
- Server-side token exhaustion and higher queueing leading to a mix of 429s and timeouts.

Immediate actions we've taken (now):
1) Applied a soft throttle on the FederalGrid key to stabilize the platform (this returns fast 429s when traffic exceeds the emergency threshold).
2) Deployed an edge circuit-breaker to automatically reject sustained high-error traffic and avoid queue backpressure.
3) Temporarily increased capacity on the serving tier to absorb legitimate traffic while the situation stabilizes.

Recommended steps for FederalGrid (please implement now if possible):
- If you can, reduce concurrency on the workers that call Redwood for 30 minutes.
- Upgrade to Redwood SDK v1.2.3 (we will publish today) which changes default retry behavior to exponential backoff with jitter and reduces max retries.
- If upgrading is not immediate, insert this patch in your caller logic (example):
  - exponential backoff base=200ms, max_backoff=5s, add full jitter, max_retries=3

We plan to follow up with a short RCA and a permanent SDK change. Monica will schedule a postmortem/RTC with your engineering team. I realize the soft throttle may cause some calls to be rejected — we set thresholds conservatively to preserve overall service health. If you want us to roll back throttle more quickly, we can discuss tradeoffs.

We'll keep monitoring and I'll send another update by EOD PT.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@federalgrid.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: FederalGrid API Team <api-team@federalgrid.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 429/timeout errors from Redwood — immediate help needed

Mina / Monica — thanks for the rapid response and for the mitigation. We implemented the concurrency reduction and pushed the backoff snippet to the most critical callers; the volume dropped and client-side retries subsided. After applying the changes our success rate recovered to ~98% and latency returned to baseline.

We'll schedule the postmortem next week and would like a copy of any logs you can share (token-level request counts and timing). Also please share the planned SDK release notes and the exact patch you applied server-side so we can coordinate the timeline for a full upgrade.

Appreciate the help — the quick throttle/circuit-breaker approach prevented a much longer outage for us.

Regards,
Sarah
Head of Integrations, FederalGrid
